title: Potato Chili
description: Potato Chili is a crispy and flavorful Indo-Chinese style dish featuring golden potatoes tossed in a spicy, tangy, savory chili sauce. Fragrant dried chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, garlic, ginger, and fermented chili bean paste create layers of heat and umami, while vinegar and sugar provide a balanced sweet-sour finish.

ingredients.title: For the Potato
items: Potatoes (Yukon Gold or Russet) – 500 g, peeled and cut into thin strips or bite-sized cubes
Vegetable oil – 2–3 tbsp for pan-frying, or as needed for deep-frying

ingredients.title: For the Chili Sauce
items: Dried red chilies – 2–3, broken in half
Spring onions – 2, white and green parts separated and chopped
Doubanjiang (fermented chili bean paste) – 1 tbsp (optional but recommended)
Chinese black vinegar or rice vinegar – 1 tbsp

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Potatoes
steps: Wash and peel the potatoes, then cut them into thin strips or small cubes for a restaurant-style presentation.
Soak the cut potatoes in cold water for 20–30 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain and pat the potatoes completely dry.
Toss the potatoes evenly with cornstarch and salt.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Frying the Potatoes
steps: For deep-frying, heat oil to 180°C (350°F) and fry the potatoes until golden and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
For pan-frying, heat 2–3 tbsp vegetable oil in a non-stick pan and shallow-fry the potatoes, turning frequently, until golden and crisp.
For an extra-crispy texture, double-fry the potatoes or briefly fry them again before tossing with the sauce.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Preparing the Chili Sauce
steps: Heat a wok or large pan over medium heat and add a small amount of oil.
Add the dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and toast for 20–30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Add minced garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the spring onions. Stir-fry for about 30 seconds until aromatic.
Add doubanjiang and fry for another 20–30 seconds to release its flavor.
Stir in soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water or stock. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Combining & Finishing
steps: Add the crispy potatoes to the chili sauce.
Toss quickly over high heat until the potatoes are evenly coated while retaining as much crispness as possible.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with the green parts of the spring onions.
Serve immediately while the potatoes are hot and crisp.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve immediately as a spicy appetizer or side dish.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds or finely chopped coriander for extra flavor and visual appeal.
Pair with steamed rice or other Indo-Chinese dishes for a complete meal.
For a protein-rich version, add thinly sliced chicken, beef, or tofu.

chefTips: Double-frying the potatoes, or frying them and briefly tossing them in a very hot pan, helps maintain their crisp texture after adding the sauce.
Balance the sweet, sour, spicy, and umami flavors carefully by adjusting the sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, and chili paste.
Make sure the potatoes are thoroughly dry before coating with cornstarch to achieve better browning and crispness.
Do not overcook the potatoes after adding the sauce, as prolonged cooking will make them soft.
Use Sichuan peppercorns for an authentic numbing, aromatic character, but omit them if a cleaner chili flavor is preferred.
Add garnishes just before serving to preserve their freshness and presentation.
